---
title: "Cleaning data: Finn the Wolfhound"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(here)
library(tidyr)
library(gutenbergr) 
```

Use this document to work on cleaning your data and adding any additional variables that may be relevant.

You can also add other files if it will help to organize your process (see the quakersaints-example)

### loading data to check if tokonizations was succesful 
```{r load-data}

if (!dir.exists(here("data"))) {
  dir.create(here("data"))
}

if (!file.exists(here("data/finn.rda"))) {
     finn <- gutenberg_download(30550)
     save(finn, file=here("data/finn.rda"))
} else {
     load(here("data/finn.rda"))
}
```

What I see here is that while the table of contents says

> CHAPTER XXXIII. Back from the Wild

The text says 
>BACK FROM THE WILD
on line 10863.
So to match up the titles from the table of contents 
to the chapters you will need to  chop off everything
up to the "." in the table of contents. 
Then change them to upper case.

```{r}
# Get the TOC lines
toc <- finn |> 
  mutate(line_number = row_number()) |>
  filter(line_number %in% 33:97) |>
  filter(text != "") 

# Clean the titles and assign a Chapter Number
toc_clean <- toc |> 
  mutate(
    # Keep your great regex to grab the title
    title = str_extract(text, "(?<=\\.).*") |> toupper() |> trimws(),
    # Because the TOC is in perfect order, row 1 is Ch 1, row 2 is Ch 2!
    chapter_number = row_number() 
  ) |>
  # Keep only what we need for the join
  select(chapter_number, chapter_title = title)

head(toc_clean)
```
```{r}
# Get the TOC lines
toc <- finn |> 
  mutate(line_number = row_number()) |>
  filter(line_number %in% 33:97) |>
  filter(text != "") 

# Clean the titles and assign a Chapter Number
toc_clean <- toc |> 
  mutate(
    # Keep your great regex to grab the title
    title = str_extract(text, "(?<=\\.).*") |> toupper() |> trimws(),
    # Because the TOC is in perfect order, row 1 is Ch 1, row 2 is Ch 2!
    chapter_number = row_number() 
  ) |>
  # Keep only what we need for the join
  select(chapter_number, chapter_title = title)

head(toc_clean)
```
Then you can add this information to the original data

```{r}
finn_organized <- finn |>
  # Clean invisible spaces
  mutate(clean_text = str_trim(text)) |>
  
  # Safely detect "Chapter I", "CHAPTER 2", etc., and count them up
  mutate(chapter_number = cumsum(str_detect(clean_text, regex("^chapter", ignore_case = TRUE)))) |>
  
  # Drop all the intro material before Chapter 1
  filter(chapter_number > 0)
finn_with_chapters <- finn_organized |>
  left_join(toc_clean, by = "chapter_number") |>
  
  # We don't even need fill() anymore because the join perfectly assigns 
  # the title to every single word in that chapter!
  select(-clean_text) # Drop our temporary cleaning column

# Save the beautifully clean, titled data!
save(finn_with_chapters, file = here("data/finn_with_chapters.rda"))

# Quick sanity check: Did we get all the chapters?
max(finn_with_chapters$chapter_number, na.rm = TRUE)
```

At this point you can save the updated file.
THen you can go back and tokenize, stem etc.
This way you can compare the chapters to each other.



```{r}
save(finn, file = here("data/finn_with_chapters.rda"))
```
